description: The bar chart illustrates the time distribution (in seconds) across four operational stages — Search, Extract, Fetch, and Retrieval — for three performance metrics: Average (Avg.), 50th percentile (50%), and 75th percentile (75%) — as part of the evaluation of the WebGLM system. The vertical axis represents time in seconds, ranging from 0.0 to 8.0 with tick marks at 2.0-second intervals. Each group of stacked bars corresponds to one of the three metrics along the horizontal axis, with bars sorted left to right as Avg., 50%, and 75%. Within each group, the stages are stacked in the order: Search (dark blue, bottom), Extract (medium blue), Fetch (light blue), and Retrieval (very light blue, top), as indicated by the legend. For the Avg. case, Search takes approximately 1.8 sec, Extract ~2.2 sec, Fetch ~0.8 sec, and Retrieval ~0.7 sec, totaling ~5.5 sec. At the 50% percentile, Search is ~1.5 sec, Extract ~1.8 sec, Fetch ~0.6 sec, and Retrieval ~0.5 sec, summing to ~4.4 sec. At the 75% percentile, Search is ~1.7 sec, Extract ~2.3 sec, Fetch ~0.7 sec, and Retrieval ~0.6 sec, totaling ~5.3 sec. The 75% bar is visually emphasized with a gray background, indicating it represents a higher latency threshold. The chart demonstrates that Extract consistently consumes the most time across all percentiles, followed by Search, while Fetch and Retrieval contribute smaller, relatively stable portions.
